The Question: Are all earned titles always active?
Option B: Collect many - equip a limited set
Recommendation: DECIDED - 10 equip slots
Why: Equip slots turn titles into build choices and make every new title interesting forever. 10 is generous enough to feel like a real character sheet.
Knock-on Effects: Needs equip UI - needs modifier add/remove on swap - see the Balance Model sheet for the cap that makes 10 slots safe

The Question: If there are 10 slots what stops a player equipping 10 Legendaries?
Option B: A point budget across equipped titles
Recommendation: DECIDED - 40-point budget cap on top of the 10 slots
Why: 10 Legendary titles is roughly 95 points - about +100% damage and +20 hearts. Slots are the shape of the build. The budget is the actual limiter. Early players are never constrained by it because they do not own enough titles yet - it only bites exactly when it needs to.
Knock-on Effects: Equip handler must reject over-budget equips server-side. UI shows "31 / 40" live

The Question: Do Unique and Limited titles consume a slot or budget?
Recommendation: DECIDED - budget-exempt and slot-exempt
Why: Player decision and a good one. Makes scarce titles feel genuinely special rather than a slot tax you resent.
Knock-on Effects: Only safe because of the scarce power ceiling below - do not ship one without the other

The Question: How strong can a budget-exempt title be?
Option A: As strong as its rarity suggests
Option B: Capped low with a signature power instead
Recommendation: DECIDED - max 5 points of raw stats each
Why: Without this the exemption breaks the whole model. A veteran holding 9 scarce titles would carry ~90 free points and the 40-point budget would be decoration. Scarce titles earn their status through a signature ability and public prestige - not big numbers.
Knock-on Effects: All 9 scarce titles in the Titles sheet were re-specced to this rule

The Question: Can a player dump the whole budget into one stat?
Recommendation: DECIDED - hard caps on the Titles-sourced total - see Balance Model
Why: Second safety net. Clamps the total this mod contributes - equipped plus scarce - NOT the player's final attribute value. Stacked damage resistances approaching immunity is the classic way this genre breaks.
Knock-on Effects: Clamp at modifier-application time not at equip time. Apply one modifier per attribute and never read the player's final attribute value.

The Question: How does scarcity work with one player?
Option B: Same code path - the ledger just has one player
Recommendation: DECIDED - same code path
Why: SP runs an integrated server so server-authoritative logic works identically with zero special casing. Unique titles become ordinary achievements - which is fine. Nothing to build and nothing to test twice.
Knock-on Effects: Write everything server-side and SP is free. Add a config toggle to hide scarcity UI in SP if it reads oddly

The Question: What does the random first-join title do?
Option B: Random from the Common and Uncommon pool only
Recommendation: Weighted roll over Common..Legendary using the rarity weights
Why: Small chance of something great is the hook. Rolling a Mythic on join devalues the whole ladder
Knock-on Effects: Must exclude Unique/Limited titles from the roll or first-joiners hoard the scarce ones

The Question: What happens when a Limited holder stops playing?
Recommendation: DECIDED - held forever. Nothing is ever released
Why: Player decision - titles are never revoked. Losing a 150-day deathless grind because you took a month off is exactly the feel-bad this sheet warns about elsewhere. The cost is that latecomers on an old server cannot chase a filled Limited title - accepted. Raise the holder cap in the server config if a title fills up too fast
Knock-on Effects: No last-seen sweep needed at all - the ledger becomes append-only which is simpler and crash-safer

The Question: Should any title be stealable?
Recommendation: Yes but only 1-2 Mythic ones
Why: Rivalry is fun in small doses. Broadly applied it makes the mod feel punishing
Knock-on Effects: Needs a transfer event - a broadcast - and a grace period so it does not ping-pong

The Question: Can you lose an earned title?
Recommendation: DECIDED - NEVER - for every scarcity type
Why: Revocable titles feel awful and create save-scumming. A title is a record of something you did - the deed does not stop having happened
Knock-on Effects: Sole exception is the Contested type - currently The Unrivaled alone - where being overtaken IS the mechanic. Everything else survives death and inactivity forever

The Question: How strong is a fully-kitted player?
Recommendation: Cap total equipped power budget - see the Rarity sheet
Why: Without a cap you will not notice the mod is broken until someone posts a video
Knock-on Effects: Enforce in code - refuse to equip past the cap - do not rely on discipline

The Question: Do scarce titles create toxicity?
Recommendation: Design against it
Why: Limited and Unique titles are the best idea in this mod and the biggest risk. Keep them prestige-flavored rather than raw-power-defining
Knock-on Effects: Scarce titles should be roughly equal in power to a common title of the same rarity - the scarcity IS the reward

The Question: How do players find them?
Recommendation: Hint after partial progress
Why: Pure secrets get datamined day one and then they are just wiki chores. Hints keep discovery alive
Knock-on Effects: Needs a partial-progress notion for compound conditions

The Question: Where do titles live?
Recommendation: Datapack JSON with a codec
Why: Costs you two days up front and saves you months. Also lets modpack authors rebalance without forking
Knock-on Effects: Effects need a registry of effect types with codecs. This is the single best architectural investment here

The Question: How many bespoke effects?
Recommendation: Primitives - CUSTOM only for Legendary+
Why: 60 bespoke effects is 60 things that break every game update. Attribute-based effects survive updates almost for free
Knock-on Effects: The Effect Catalog sheet is your primitive list

The Question: Build a custom stat system?
Recommendation: Reuse both
Why: Vanilla already tracks blocks mined per block and mobs killed per type per player and persists it. Advancements are already a JSON condition engine. Reusing them removes most of your backend
Knock-on Effects: Custom counters only for what vanilla genuinely cannot express

The Question: Do titles survive death?
Recommendation: Yes - always
Why: Losing a grind to a creeper would end the mod's goodwill instantly
Knock-on Effects: On Forge you must copy the record yourself in PlayerEvent.Clone - there is no copyOnDeath flag until the port. Test it - this is a classic silent bug

The Question: Can you earn titles in creative?
Recommendation: No by default - configurable
Why: Otherwise every title is a five-minute creative session
Knock-on Effects: Also gate on gamemode changes mid-progress

The Question: Modded blocks and mobs count?
Recommendation: Yes via tags
Why: Writing conditions against minecraft:stone instead of the stone tag means the mod is dead in any modpack
Knock-on Effects: Use tags everywhere in conditions and in damage-vs-type checks

The Question: What admin tools?
Recommendation: Full - plus a ledger inspection command
Why: Server admins will need to fix things and you will need it for testing on day one
Knock-on Effects: /titles grant / revoke / list / ledger / reset - all op-gated

The Question: Which Minecraft version and loader do we build for first?
Recommendation: DECIDED - 1.20.1 on Forge 47.x
Why: Every mod we want to integrate with ships Forge 1.20.1 only. Integration is the single requirement that cannot be solved in code - everything else can. 1.20.1 also still has one of the two largest modded player bases so this is not an exile to a dead version.
Knock-on Effects: Overrides the earlier NeoForge-only decision. Costs us Java 17 - obfuscated mappings - Capabilities instead of Attachments - and ForgeGradle. The eventual port crosses a loader change and five years of API churn at once.

The Question: How do we get from 1.20.1 to modern?
Option B: One jump from a finished 1.20.1 to current stable
Recommendation: DECIDED - one jump - skip every intermediate
Why: Intermediate versions have no meaningful player base. Porting five times multiplies the worst breaking-change era in modding history by five. Port once - with a shipped and playtested mod in hand rather than a half-built one.
Knock-on Effects: Two long-lived branches only. Cherry-pick forward from 1.20.1. Do NOT keep a shared main that merges into both - with this much API divergence that is a permanent merge-conflict tax.

The Question: How do we make the eventual port cheap?
Recommendation: DECIDED - codecs everywhere - never hand-write NBT
Why: Codecs exist in 1.20.1 and survive the whole span to 26.x essentially unchanged. Highest-value forward-compat rule on this sheet and it costs nothing to follow from day one.
Knock-on Effects: Applies to title JSON - player data - packets and the scarcity ledger alike. No exceptions.

The Question: Where does player state actually live?
Option B: In a plain record that the Capability merely holds
Recommendation: DECIDED - codec-backed record - capability is a thin holder
Why: Forge Capabilities do not exist on NeoForge 26.x - Data Attachments replace them outright. If the state lives in a POJO the port swaps the holder and the data is untouched. If the state lives in the capability the port is a rewrite.
Knock-on Effects: Same rule for the per-world ledger. SavedData does survive the port but keep its payload a codec-backed record regardless.

The Question: What shape are packets?
Option B: Records with a codec plus a handle(player) method
Recommendation: DECIDED - packet records with codecs
Why: 1.20.2 rewrote networking wholesale. SimpleChannel registration is roughly ten lines of glue we throw away - the payload-based system on 26.x wants nearly the same record shape underneath it.
Knock-on Effects: Keep every bit of packet handling logic out of the registration glue. The glue should do nothing but wire things up.

The Question: How do we key attribute modifiers?
Option B: A ResourceLocation-shaped id in the title JSON
Recommendation: DECIDED - id in JSON - derive the 1.20.1 UUID from it
Why: 1.20.1 keys attribute modifiers by UUID - modern versions key them by ResourceLocation. Derive the UUID with UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes over the id string and the content files never need touching at port time.
Knock-on Effects: Every title JSON carries a stable modifier id. The derivation is one small utility method that gets deleted at the port.

The Question: Do we ever touch item NBT?
Recommendation: DECIDED - never touch item NBT
Why: 1.20.5 replaced item NBT with data components and that is the nastiest single migration in the range. This mod is player-data-driven so it may never need item data at all. Stay that way on purpose rather than by accident.
Knock-on Effects: If a title effect ever appears to need item NBT - find another route or raise it here as a decision before writing it.

The Question: How much Forge do we let into the codebase?
Option A: Use it freely - it is our loader
Option B: Confine it behind a small platform layer
Recommendation: DECIDED - confine it - five or six interfaces
Why: Forge to NeoForge renames every package - reshapes the event bus - and deletes Capabilities. Every direct Forge call is a port cost. Every call behind an interface is one adapter rewrite instead of hundreds of scattered edits.
Knock-on Effects: Registration - networking - persistence - events - attributes - screen glue. Stop there. Do not build an abstraction for something with exactly one implementation and no second one on the horizon.

The Question: How do we depend on the Forge mods we integrate with?
Option B: Soft dependency with one isolated compat class each
Recommendation: DECIDED - soft dependencies behind mod-loaded guards
Why: A hard dependency means our mod refuses to load without theirs and breaks every time they update. Isolated compat classes also let the port drop any integration whose mod never reached 26.x without touching core code.
Knock-on Effects: Core must load and play correctly with every integration absent. Test that case explicitly - it is the common one for most users.

The Question: Do our caps limit our own contribution or the player's final stat?
Option A: Clamp the player's final attribute value
Recommendation: DECIDED - clamp only the Titles-sourced total
Why: Every pack we target already grants attributes - Just Leveling and Passive Skill Tree in Soulrend - skill tree and divine blessings in Cisco's. Clamping the final value would grant nothing in those packs or actively strip health another mod gave - a bug report blaming us for their mod. We stack on top and stay out of the way.
Knock-on Effects: Attribute code must never call player.getAttributeValue() to make a decision. Sum our own effects - clamp - apply. The derived-UUID rule from Forward compat - attribute ids is what makes our modifiers identifiable.
